As of 2024, U.S. imports of components such as electric motors, hydraulic power units, gear assemblies, valves, and control instruments generally faced base import duties of 1.5%–4% (U.S. International Trade Commission 2025a), depending on the specific product and country of origin. Imports from partner countries such as Canada, Mexico, and South Korea typically qualified for zero tariffs under free trade agreements such as the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement (USMCA) and the Korea Free Trade Agreement. However, products originating from China could incur an additional 25% tariff under Section 301. Tracker components with steel or aluminum housings could also be subject to Section 232 measures, while in certain cases AD/CVD duties were applied on top of the base Most Favored Nation tariffs to select gear parts, bearings, and valves from countries such as China, India, and South Korea. 4.3 Torque Tubes This section focuses on the production of torque tubes in the PV tracker supply chain, including direct inputs. Figure 50 shows a simplified supply chain diagram for torque tube production. 74 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Within most single-axis tracker systems, torque tubes are the central rotating shafts that support and—powered by the system’s actuators—drive the movement of PV modules along a single axis. The torque tubes can be manufactured by tracker manufacturers, imported, or manufactured by third-party U.S. roll formers. Torque tubes must meet strict mechanical tolerance requirements to enable trouble-free bearing rotation and proper system alignment as well as structural integrity requirements to withstand dynamic and static loads, such as wind and snow, without mechanical flaws. They are typically made from galvanized steel for durability and corrosion resistance.
